newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway cuts key rate by 25 b.p. to 3.25 pct.
newsitem.headline: Norway cuts key rate by 25 b.p. to 3.25 pct.

text.p: Norway's central bank on Friday cut its overnight deposit rate for commercial and savings banks by 25 basis points to 3.25 percent, the second cut in three days in an attempt to control the sharply appreciating crown.
In addition to cutting the deposit rate, the central bank said it was reducing the overnight lending rate by 25 basis points to 5.25 percent.
Both measures were with immediate effect.
The deposit rate normally sets the floor for money market rates and the overnight lending rate sets the ceiling.
The bank on Wednesday announced a 50 basis point reduction in both rates effective Thursday in a fruitless effort to curb the steady rise of the currency.
Undeterred by the cut in official interest rates, the crown powered to its strongest level in more than six years on Thursday on what dealers described as speculative buying.

It outperformed the inverse ECU index of European currencies for the first time. It appreciated from 100.64 on the index shortly before the cut was announced after Norwegian markets closed on Wednesday to 99.89 when they shut on Thursday.
On Friday, after the latest announcement, the crown continued to surge ahead and stood at 98.98 at 0830 GMT.

Analysts say the crown is undervalued as the Norwegian economy is booming with huge surpluses in the national budget and current account. Norway is the world's second biggest oil exporter after Saudi Arabia.
